summary: Returns the value as a boolean, or throws.
description: Only the two primitives pass. `new Boolean(false)` is an object, and the strings `"true"` and `"false"` are strings.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as a boolean.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is not a boolean.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireBoolean(true); // => true
requireBoolean(false); // => false
requireBoolean("true"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireBoolean(1); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
